title: Returning a faulty phone
context: You bought a phone two weeks ago and the screen is faulty. You are in the shop.

a.speaker: Assistant
a.say: Good afternoon. How can I help?

choices.text: Hello. I bought this phone two weeks ago and the screen has stopped working. I'd like a refund, please.
This phone is rubbish!
choices.feedback: Complaining without details makes it harder to get help.

choices.text: I think there's a problem with this phone. Could you take a look?
choices.feedback: Polite, but state what you want.

b1.speaker: Assistant
b1.say: I am sorry about that. Do you have the receipt?

choices.text: Yes, here it is. It's dated the ninth.
I've lost it, but I paid by card. Could you check the transaction?
No. Why do you need it?

b2.speaker: Assistant
b2.say: I understand you are upset. Could you tell me what exactly is wrong?

choices.text: I'm sorry. The screen went black after a week and won't turn on.
Just give me my money back.

b3.speaker: Assistant
b3.say: Of course. What seems to be the problem?

choices.text: The screen has stopped working, so I would like a refund or a replacement.
It doesn't work.

c1.speaker: Assistant
c1.say: Thank you. I can offer a full refund or a replacement. Which would you prefer?

choices.text: A replacement, please, if you have one in stock.
I'd prefer a refund, thank you.
Whatever.

c2.speaker: Assistant
c2.say: Without a receipt I would need a manager to approve it. It may take ten minutes.

choices.text: That's fine, I'll wait. Thank you for your help.
This is ridiculous. I have no time.
Could you call me when the manager has decided? I can leave my number.

end.speaker: Assistant
end.say: Thank you for your patience. Is there anything else I can do for you?

title: Sharing a flat: a disagreement
context: Your flatmate keeps leaving dirty dishes in the sink. You want to talk about it.

choices.text: Yes. I'd like to talk about the dishes. Is now a good time?
You never clean up!
Nothing, forget it.
choices.feedback: Avoiding the issue will not solve it.

choices.text: There are often dirty dishes in the sink, and it's becoming a problem for me.
You're so lazy.

b2.speaker: Flatmate
b2.say: That's not fair. I've been very busy lately.

choices.text: I understand you're busy. Could we agree on a simple rota?
choices.feedback: Acknowledges the other view, then proposes a solution.

choices.text: I don't care. Clean them now.

b3.speaker: Flatmate
b3.say: Are you sure? You seem annoyed.

choices.text: Well, actually, yes. It's about the dishes.
I'm fine.

c.speaker: Flatmate
c.say: OK, you're right. What do you suggest?

choices.text: How about we each wash our own dishes the same evening?
You do all of them from now on.
choices.feedback: Not very fair; aim for compromise.

end.speaker: Flatmate
end.say: Alright. Let's try that and see how it goes.
